newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: ABU DHABI SPENDS $2 BLN ON PROJECTS IN 1996.
newsitem.headline: ABU DHABI SPENDS $2 BLN ON PROJECTS IN 1996.

text.p: The oil-rich emirate of Abu Dhabi spent over $2 billion on public projects in the United Arab Emirates in 1996, official figures showed.

The figures by the Planning Department, obtained by Reuters on Thursday, showed total spending by Abu Dhabi last year was 7.6 billion dirhams ($2.07 billion) in 1996, less than the budgeted 11.9 billion dirhams.

They showed spending on projects within the emirate, one of seven that make up the UAE, reached seven billion dirhams out of an allocated 10.64 billion. Spending on federal projects stood at 619.2 million dirhams out of the budgeted 1.26 billion dirhams.
Financial analysts in Abu Dhabi, the richest of the seven emirates, said for the first time since 1992 spending in 1996 was less than what had been budgeted for.
They said that was largely due to delays in payments to projects until their completion.
Official figures show spending in 1995 was 8.8 billion dirhams compared to a budgeted 8.2 billion dirhams.
